Seismic Data Processing

Our processing workflows are specifically designed to preserve amplitude fidelity and phase characteristics essential for quantitative interpretation. Unlike conventional processing, we prioritize the attributes that matter for reservoir characterization.

Amplitude-Preserving Processing

Careful treatment of gains, filters, and corrections to maintain relative amplitude relationships critical for AVO analysis.

Pre-Stack Processing

Offset-dependent processing and angle gathers optimized for simultaneous inversion applications.

Wavelet Estimation

Statistical and deterministic wavelet extraction for accurate tie to well data and inversion conditioning.

Technical Foundation

Our processing approach is grounded in the physics of wave propagation. We apply corrections based on established theory:

  • - Geometric spreading: Compensated using known velocity models and spherical divergence corrections
  • - Attenuation (Q): Inverse-Q filtering based on measured or estimated quality factors
  • - NMO stretch: Careful mute design to avoid frequency distortion at far offsets
  • - Migration aperture: Optimized for target depth and structural complexity

Feasibility Studies

Before committing resources to a full interpretation project, understand whether seismic data can actually resolve your targets. Our feasibility studies use forward modeling to quantify what is detectable given your specific geological and seismic conditions.

This approach is scientifically rigorous because it works forward from known physics: we start with measured rock properties, apply established rock physics models, and compute the expected seismic response. The result is an objective assessment of detectability.

Key Questions Answered:

  • Can porosity variations be distinguished from lithology changes?
  • Is the hydrocarbon effect separable from brine response?
  • What is the minimum detectable thickness or property contrast?

Lithofacies Prediction

Transform seismic attributes into geological rock types using statistical classification methods calibrated to well data. Our approach provides not just a single answer, but probability distributions that quantify prediction uncertainty.

Bayesian Classification

Statistical framework that incorporates prior geological knowledge with seismic observations to compute posterior probabilities for each facies.

Neural Network Methods

Supervised learning algorithms trained on well control to recognize complex, non-linear relationships between seismic and facies.

Cross-Validation

Blind well testing to objectively assess prediction accuracy before applying models to undrilled areas.

Scientific Basis

Lithofacies prediction is grounded in the physical relationship between rock composition and seismic response:

Elastic Property Separation

Different minerals (quartz, feldspar, clay, calcite) have distinct elastic moduli and densities that manifest as separable clusters in impedance space.

Vp/Vs Discrimination

Shale typically exhibits higher Vp/Vs than sand at similar porosity, enabling lithology discrimination through simultaneous inversion.

Probabilistic Framework

Results are expressed as probabilities, acknowledging that seismic data cannot uniquely determine lithology - uncertainty quantification is built in.

Service

Inversion to Reservoir Properties

The ultimate goal of quantitative interpretation: transform seismic data into estimates of the reservoir properties that drive economic decisions - porosity, net pay, fluid saturation.

Acoustic Impedance Inversion

Post-stack inversion to estimate P-impedance (Vp x density), the fundamental elastic property most directly related to seismic amplitude.

Based on convolutional model: Seismic = Wavelet * Reflectivity

Simultaneous AVO Inversion

Pre-stack inversion exploiting angle-dependent reflectivity (Aki-Richards approximation) to independently estimate P-impedance, S-impedance, and density.

Zoeppritz equations linearized for practical application

Extended Elastic Impedance

Generalized impedance formulation (Whitcombe et al.) optimized for specific rock property discrimination at any projection angle.

Angle rotation to maximize target sensitivity

Rock Physics Transforms

Convert elastic properties to reservoir properties (porosity, Vclay, Sw) using calibrated rock physics relationships derived from well data.

Empirical calibration with theoretical constraints

Stochastic Inversion

Generate multiple equally-probable realizations that honor both seismic and well data, capturing geological variability below seismic resolution.

Geostatistical simulation with seismic constraint

Uncertainty Quantification

Propagate seismic noise, wavelet uncertainty, and rock physics scatter through inversion to deliver confidence intervals on property estimates.

Monte Carlo and analytical error propagation
Service

Rock Physics Analysis

Rock physics provides the theoretical link between reservoir properties (what we want to know) and seismic response (what we measure). This is the scientific foundation that makes quantitative interpretation possible.

We apply established theoretical models, calibrated to your specific geological setting, to understand how changes in porosity, fluid content, or lithology will manifest in seismic data.

Explore SeisTool Software

Theoretical Framework

Gassmann Fluid Substitution

Predicts how bulk modulus changes with pore fluid composition at low frequencies. The foundation for DHI analysis and time-lapse interpretation.

Hertz-Mindlin Contact Theory

Models pressure-dependent elastic properties of granular media. Essential for understanding seismic velocity changes with depth and effective stress.

Hashin-Shtrikman Bounds

Theoretical limits on effective elastic moduli for composite materials. Provides physics-based constraints on mixing relationships.

Inclusion Models (Kuster-Toksoz, DEM)

Account for pore geometry effects on elastic properties. Critical for carbonates and fractured reservoirs where pore shape matters.
